rounds.text: Allied Digital Services Ltd trades at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 1.41x against a book value of ₹ 83.8 [E1], and its P/B multiple of 1.05x represents a substantial discount to the sector benchmark of 3.08x [E6]. The business demonstrates robust top-line expansion, registering a 32% compounded sales growth rate over 5 years and 23% over 3 years [E14, E15], supported by a favorable information technology sector tailwind with a tailwind score of up to +0.65 [E63]. Furthermore, the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.26x [E34], while also showing positive quarterly sales momentum [E56]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed significantly alongside negative operating cash flows and low return metrics [E26, E31, E53].

Allied Digital Services Ltd suffers from a severe collapse in operational profitability, evidenced by an annual operating margin of just 1% in March 2026—a steep decline of 9 percentage points from three years prior [E26]—and a quarterly operating margin plunging to -28% [E27]. This deteriorating profitability cascades directly into shareholder returns, with ROE sitting at -0.8% [E12], ROCE at 1.2% [E11], and a 10-year median ROE of only 2% [E22]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has cratered by -130% [E17], and net profits dropped by -375% YoY [E58], completely disconnecting valuation from fundamental delivery despite a P/E of 18.1x [E5] and a rules-based screen score of just 32 out of 100 indicating a medium-confidence sell [E55]. The company is simultaneously burning through cash at an alarming rate, registering a negative operating cash flow of Rs -40 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -50 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], which has forced borrowings up substantially to Rs 121 Cr from Rs 67 Cr a year earlier [E35]. Compounded share price growth reflects this underlying distress, down -31% over the past year [E21] alongside negative institutional money flow [E40] and a price resting comfortably below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. Conceded: [E14, E63].

While the bear points to collapsing operational profitability and a negative trailing profit growth of -130% [E17, E26], the business maintains strong multi-year compounding sales growth of 32% over 5 years and 23% over 3 years [E14, E15], supported by quarterly sales growth QoQ [E56] and operating inside a robust Information Technology sector tailwind of +0.65 [E63]. The bear highlights rising borrowings to Rs 121 Cr [E35], but debt to equity remains at a conservatively financed 0.26x [E34]. Furthermore, while the bear cites a low P/E multiple context and weak recent returns [E5, E12], the stock trades at an attractive price-to-book of 1.41x on a book value of ₹ 83.8 [E1] and commands a favorable P/B of 1.05x compared to the sector benchmark of 3.08x [E6]. Conceded: [E27, E31, E32].

Conceded: [E14, E15, E56, E63]. While multi-year sales growth looks attractive, top-line expansion is completely failing to translate into fundamental value, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth collapse of -130% and a net profit drop of -375% year-over-year [E17, E58]. The bull's reliance on a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x [E34] ignores the reality that total borrowings jumped sharply from Rs 67 Cr to Rs 121 Cr [E35], creating a low interest coverage ratio flag [E52] alongside severely negative operating cash flow of Rs -40 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -50 Cr [E31, E32]. Pointing to an attractive price-to-book ratio of 1.05x against the sector [E6] misses the structural destruction of capital shown by a long-term median return on equity of just 2% and a current ROE of -0.8% [E8, E22, E23]. Finally, the supportive sector tailwind cannot overcome company-specific operational decay where quarterly operating margins have plummeted to -28% [E27] and institutional money flow registers as negative [E40].
